relatedSnapshot.title: Pre-warmed domain checkout retry can cancel paid order after Autumn subscription exists
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Yes

EVIDENCE:

* Support investigation for Intercom conversation 215474831432769 found customer order `<uuid>` paid successfully in Stripe for `$84.00` at 2026-06-24 17:30 UTC, receipt `2736-7406`, charge `py_3TlubOGPuqjknq341kmSW0B1`.
* Prod DB shows the order ended `status = refunded`, `domains_provisioned = 0`, `inboxes_provisioned = 0`, with no `mail_domain` / `mail_inbox` rows for the selected domains.
* Axiom shows repeated checkout retries after payment failed with `subscription_id '<domain>' is already in use for this customer`, then reservations were released and reconcile marked the order refunded because paid balance existed but reservations were missing.
* Stripe shows `amount_refunded = 0`; cancellation left `$84` as customer credit (`customer.balance = -8400`) rather than provisioning the purchased domains/inboxes or issuing a card refund.

POTENTIAL FIX:

* In the pre-warmed domain checkout initiation/retry path, treat Autumn `subscription_id ... is already in use for this customer` as a signal that the checkout/subscription may already exist and route to payment confirmation/reconciliation instead of surfacing checkout creation failure.
* Prevent a pending/cancel action from releasing reservations when Stripe/Autumn indicates the order has already been paid or corresponding subscriptions exist.
* Add a targeted regression test around retrying `initiateDomainPurchaseCheckout` after a successful Autumn multiAttach/Stripe payment but before `confirmDomainPurchase` has marked the order paid.

WHATS NEEDED TO RESOLVE:

* Reproduce the payment retry state with mocked Autumn multiAttach returning duplicate subscription ID after an initial successful payment.
* Patch checkout confirmation/reconcile behavior so paid orders cannot be cancelled/released due to duplicate subscription IDs.
* Decide customer remediation separately: provision 2 domains + 6 inboxes using existing credit, or issue an actual Stripe refund.

relatedSnapshot.title: Domains in failed/Error state have no Cancel option, leaving active inboxes uncancellable
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Yes

EVIDENCE:

* Customer: Name 5 (<email>), workspace **Company One** (`<workspace-slug>`, org `<uuid>`). Reports domains/inboxes still active after cancelling, and no Cancel button in Settings -> Billing -> Email Accounts & Domains.
* Prod DB: Company One has 12 `mail_domain` rows across 2 DFY orders.
  * 6 are `suspended` / "Cancelled by user" (updated 2026-07-20 14:36) - his cancellation on Jul 20 worked for these.
  * 6 are `failed` / "Name 6 waiting for domain/mailboxes": `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`, `<domain>`.
* Those failed domains still have **15** `mail_inbox` **rows with** `status = active`**,** `connected = true` (3 per domain; the 3 on <domain> are already `error`). Provisioning was recorded as failed at the domain level but the mailboxes exist and are live.
* Root cause in UI: `apps/web/components/billing/email-accounts-domains-card.tsx:44` - `const CANCELLABLE_DOMAIN_STATUSES = ['pending', 'active', 'partial']`. Domains with status `failed` render as "Error" but `isCancellable` is false, so there is no per-domain **Cancel** button and they are excluded from **Cancel all**. No self-serve path exists to remove them or their still-live inboxes.
* Orders: `<uuid>` (status `completed`, "Provisioned 2/6 domains, 6/18 inboxes") and `<uuid>` (status `requires_attention`, "Provisioned 4/6 domains, 12/18 inboxes").
* Billing (Autumn customer `<uuid>` / Stripe `<stripe-id>`): products `Domain` (qty 12) and `Inbox (DFY)` (qty 12) are `past_due` with `canceled_at = 2026-07-20`, current period end **2026-08-18**. $108/mo charge attempts have been failing since 2026-07-18 (8 declines through 2026-07-29).
* Separate question in the same conversation: the **$297 charged 2026-07-27** is the monthly **Pro** plan on a different workspace, **"Test 1"** (`<workspace-slug>`, billing account `<uuid>`, Stripe `<stripe-id>`), billed monthly since 2025-11-27. Not an Company One charge.

POTENTIAL FIX:

* Make provisioning-`failed` domains removable: either add `failed` to `CANCELLABLE_DOMAIN_STATUSES` with a cancel path that also tears down inboxes still `active`/`connected` under that domain, or surface a distinct "Remove" action for error-state domains.
* Reconcile domain vs inbox state: a `failed` domain should not keep `active`, `connected` inboxes. Add a reconciliation job plus a backfill for existing rows.

WHATS NEEDED TO RESOLVE:

* Engineering decision on the cancel/removal path for `failed` domains.
* Manual cleanup for Company One now: remove the 6 failed domains and their 15 active inboxes.
* Confirm no further billing for Company One after 2026-08-18.
* Reply to the customer on the $297 charge (Pro plan on the "Test 1" workspace).

DOCS GAP: The Help Center billing docs (`apps/web/content/docs/workspace-settings/billing.mdx`, "Email Accounts & Domains") describe **Cancel** / **Cancel all** but never explain that domains in an **Error** state show no Cancel button, why, or that support must remove them. Fin AI gave the customer cancel steps he could not follow before handing off.
CUSTOMER CONTEXT: Customer tried to cancel his workspace, emails and domains; the remaining billed items were error-state domains with no Cancel control, so he assumed cancellation had not worked.
SUGGESTED CONTENT: Add an FAQ - "Why is there no Cancel option next to my domain?" - covering the Error/failed provisioning state, its billing impact, and how to get it removed. Also add a note that each workspace bills separately and how to identify which workspace a charge belongs to.

relatedSnapshot.title: Name 2 'Remove domain' button gated on owned-domains lookup, blocking manual custom domain removal
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

The "Remove domain" button in the Name 2's custom-domain setup is disabled whenever the owned-domains (purchased domains) lookup has not completed successfully, so a customer who typed in a wrong manual domain cannot remove it and is stuck.

## Problem

A customer adds a wrong custom domain during the Name 2's custom-domain setup flow, then cannot remove or edit it: the "Remove domain" button is greyed out and the domain field is read-only, so they cannot replace it with the correct domain.

## Root cause

In apps/web/components/ai-website-creator/publish-control.tsx, the "Remove domain" button is disabled when `!canManageCurrentDomain`. That flag requires `!ownedDomainsLookupPending && !ownedDomainsLookupFailed`, i.e. the owned-domains lookup (`listOwnedDomains`, the purchased-domains marketplace query) must complete successfully before the button enables. A manual (non-purchased) custom domain's removal should not depend on that unrelated lookup, but the gating makes it so: when the lookup fails or stays pending, the customer is locked out with no self-service path. The backend `removeCustomDomain` (apps/web/trpc/routers/website/domains.ts) would succeed if invoked.

## Blast radius

65 websites / 56 orgs currently have an unverified custom domain (custom_domain set, domain_verified=false, not deleted). Query: `SELECT COUNT(*), COUNT(DISTINCT organization_id) FROM website WHERE custom_domain IS NOT NULL AND domain_verified = false AND deleted_at IS NULL;` counted 2026-09-08. Confirmed affected: 1 org.

## Proposed fix

Enable removal of a manual custom domain without requiring the owned-domains lookup to succeed. Treat a failed or pending owned-domains lookup as "not an owned domain" for the purpose of enabling the remove path (or otherwise decouple manual-domain removal from the purchased-domains query).

## What's included

The gating fix in publish-control.tsx. Excluded: a Help Center docs gap on how to remove a manual custom domain (tracked separately).

## Regression seam

In publish-control.tsx, with a manual custom domain set (unverified) and the owned-domains lookup failing or pending, the "Remove domain" button should still be enabled and trigger `removeCustomDomain`.

## Done when

* The "Remove domain" button is enabled for a manual custom domain regardless of the owned-domains lookup state.
* Removing a manual custom domain clears custom_domain and falls back to the deployment URL.
* A regression test proves the button enables when the owned-domains lookup fails or is pending.

## Reports

* ENG-13575

relatedSnapshot.title: DFY domain orders that fail leave names claimed and un-cancellable, blocking re-purchase and leaving the domain store inconsistent
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Root cause

When a Done-For-You domain order fails to provision at the provider, the domain rows are written to `mail_domain` (which has a global unique index `mail_domain_domain_unique` on `domain`) and left in a `failed` or `pending` state. Those rows are never released, so they keep holding the name for the original organization. A later order for the same name throws "Unable to claim domains for this organization" at the claim step, silently drops the overlapping domains, and leaves the new order stuck in `provisioning`.

Separately, a domain that failed still renders in Billing with no Cancel option, and the domain store availability check reads the registrar/provider (which never registered the failed name) instead of `mail_domain`. The result is a failed domain that shows as "available to purchase" while its name is actually still claimed internally.

## Evidence

* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/mail/process-create-order.ts` `processCreateColdMailOrder`: claims domains into `mail_domain` (unique on `domain`), throws "Unable to claim domains for this organization: ..." when a name is already held, and on provider failure writes domains to `status='failed'` with the order left `requires_attention` or `provisioning`.
* `apps/web/lib/inngest/functions/billing/reconcile-domain-orders-cron.ts`: retries failed inboxes on `requires_attention` orders, but does not release a domain name that failed at the provider and does not recover the duplicate-domain-claim collision.

## Blast radius (counted 2026-08-27)

Domain orders stuck in a non-terminal provisioning state: 17 `provisioning` across 17 organizations, 66 `requires_attention` across 66 organizations, 17 `failed` across 16 organizations. Done-For-You specifically: 3 `provisioning`, 26 `requires_attention`.

Domains in `failed` status with at least one `active` inbox (counted 2026-09-05): 106 domains across 41 organizations.

Paid `requires_attention` orders older than 7 days that hold `failed` domains (counted 2026-09-11): 26 orders across 25 organizations, holding 51 failed domains. Never-retried `error` inboxes on failed domains older than 7 days: 33, across 5 organizations. A 2026-09-10 count of the same cohort returned identical figures.

DFY orders stranded by a stale cross-organization `mail_domain` claim, with no saved provider order id and stale beyond 24 hours (counted 2026-09-23): 5 orders across 5 organizations and 5 users, from the ENG-14139 report. Collision cascade as of 2026-09-23: one stale failed claim is a foreign claim on 4 later DFY orders across 4 organizations, and pending claims written by two stuck orders block 4 further organizations' orders. The wider stuck-in-`provisioning` population is 9 orders across 9 organizations, of which 4 belong to ENG-13308's stall mechanism.

## Fix direction

* Release a failed domain's claim so the name can be re-purchased, and reconcile the domain store's availability check against owned-but-failed domains.
* Stop silently dropping overlapping domains from a new DFY order; fail fast with a clear message to the customer instead.

relatedSnapshot.title: Managed domain cancellation fails with a generic error when the domain and inbox order_id mismatch
relatedSnapshot.description:
## Overview

Cancelling a managed email domain from Billing → Email Accounts & Domains fails with a generic "something went wrong" error when the domain's `order_id` does not match its inboxes' `order_id`. The provider-side cancellation can still run, but the local records never update, so the domain stays active and the customer keeps being billed for a domain they want gone.

## Problem

A customer cancels a managed domain and its inboxes. The cancel returns a generic error and the domain remains active, so the customer cannot stop being billed for it.

## Root cause

`markManagedDomainCancelled` in `apps/web/lib/billing/email-management.ts` updates `mail_inbox` rows `WHERE order_id = <the domain's order_id>`. When the `mail_domain` row's `order_id` differs from its inboxes' `order_id`, zero inboxes match, and the function throws "Failed to mark managed domain inboxes as cancelled" because `expectedInboxCount > 0`. That throw is collected as a mark failure and re-thrown as "Provider cancellation completed … but failed to update local cancellation records", which `apps/web/trpc/routers/outreach/email-accounts.ts` turns into `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` "Failed to cancel selected managed domains".

## Blast radius

Confirmed: 1 org / 1 domain. Deterministic exposure: 3 orgs / 5 domains have at least one inbox whose `order_id` differs from the domain's `order_id` among cancellable (`active`/`pending`/`partial`) domains (counted 2026-09-01). Of those, 2 domains hard-fail (zero inboxes match the domain order_id) and 3 partially update.

```sql
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT md.organization_id), COUNT(DISTINCT md.id)
FROM mail_domain md
JOIN mail_inbox mi ON mi.domain_id = md.id AND mi.organization_id = md.organization_id
WHERE md.status IN ('active','pending','partial')
  AND mi.order_id IS DISTINCT FROM md.order_id;
```

## Proposed fix

Reconcile the `order_id` mismatch so a domain and its inboxes share a consistent `order_id`, and make `markManagedDomainCancelled` tolerant of the mismatch (update inboxes by `domain_id` rather than requiring `order_id` to match, or reconcile before cancelling). Add a reconciliation/backfill for existing mismatched rows.

## What's included

* Stop cancellation from hard-failing on an `order_id` mismatch.
* Backfill/reconcile existing mismatched rows.
* A regression test for the zero-match condition.

## Regression seam

`markManagedDomainCancelled` in `apps/web/lib/billing/email-management.ts`. Red: cancelling a domain whose inboxes carry a different `order_id` throws and the cancel fails. Green: the same domain cancels successfully and both the domain and its inboxes are marked cancelled.

## Done when

* Cancelling a domain with a mismatched inbox `order_id` succeeds and marks the domain and all its inboxes cancelled.
* Existing mismatched rows are reconciled.
* A regression test proves the zero-match condition no longer throws.

## Reports

* ENG-13350

relatedSnapshot.title: Domain forwarding reports success but no live redirect is ever created (coldmailreseller domains)
relatedSnapshot.description:
BUG: Yes

EVIDENCE:

* Customer Name 12 (<email>), managing client workspace **Company Five** (org <uuid>), reports that after setting up Domain Forwarding and confirming, visiting the domain shows an error page (forwarding "isn't working").
* The in-app forwarding mutation SUCCEEDS. Axiom logs (2026-07-09 17:22–17:39 UTC) for `outreach.emailAccounts.updateManagedDomainForwarding` on this org show `updatedCount: 6, failedCount: 0`, `forwardTo: <url>` — including attempts by the customer and by a support rep impersonating the account. The provider (coldmailreseller `/domains/add-forwarding`) returned success for all 6 domains.
* Despite the success, NONE of the org's 6 managed domains have any web DNS record. Checked via Name 13 DoH: apex (e.g. <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>) returns NOERROR/NODATA for A (SOA only), and `www.<domain>` returns NXDOMAIN. Zones are on Name 13 Cloud DNS (ns-cloud-*.googledomains.com). With no A record, browsers visiting the domain get a connection/DNS error — the "error page" the customer sees.
* Not isolated to this customer. Sampled coldmailreseller domains across other orgs, including ones where "Domain forwarding configured successfully" was logged today during the purchase flow (<domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>) AND months-old domains (<domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>, <domain>) — ALL have no web A record and do not resolve for web. The forward target itself (<url>) is healthy (HTTP 200).
* 2+ hours after configuration (and months for the older domains), still no record — so this is not merely DNS propagation delay.

POTENTIAL FIX:

* Investigate the coldmailreseller forwarding integration: `client.addDomainForwarding` (apps/web/lib/mail/providers/coldmailreseller/client.ts) posts to `/domains/add-forwarding` and we treat any well-formed 200 (`{status, message, data: null}`) as success. Determine whether coldmailreseller actually provisions a web redirect / DNS record for these Google-hosted domains (note their `.co` TLD is outside coldmailreseller's documented ALLOWED_TLDS of .com/.net/.org).
* If forwarding isn't actually applied, stop reporting a blanket success toast; surface the real provisioning status (or a pending/verify state) instead of "Forwarding updated for N domains." Consider verifying the redirect resolves before declaring success.

WHATS NEEDED TO RESOLVE:

* Confirm with coldmailreseller whether `/domains/add-forwarding` creates a live redirect for the affected domains/TLDs, and how long it should take.
* Decide product behavior when the provider accepts the request but the redirect never becomes live (accurate status vs. false success).

relatedSnapshot.title: Billing shows 18 purchased inboxes but Email Accounts shows 6; four of six DFY domains failed provisioning and stay billed and un-cancellable

## Testable claim

In the reported workspace, Billing -> Email Accounts & Domains lists 6 domains and 18 inboxes while Cold Email Agent -> Email Accounts lists only 6 inboxes, because four of the six Done-For-You domains (12 inboxes) failed provider provisioning and are still held in a requires_attention order, un-cancellable and still billed.

## Intercom conversation context

Reporter states (2026-09-10): the Billing settings show 6 domains with 3 emails each, but the campaign Email Accounts tab only shows 6. She expected 18, says office hours confirmed a bug, and shared screenshots. A campaign page also showed "No email accounts connected. Add one to start sending." on an Active campaign.
Conversation: <url:app.intercom.com>

## Evidence

* Production: domain_purchase_order status requires_attention, completedAt null; 6 mail_domain rows in status failed ("Domain or mailbox provisioning failed"), provisionedAt null; 12 mail_inbox rows status error, connected false, retryCount 0, lastRetryAt null; 6 mail_inbox rows active/connected. Order created 2026-08-16.
* Name 3: billing.reconcile-domain-orders-cron runs every 30 minutes and still re-attempts the same unconnected inboxes; mail_inbox.retryCount never advances.
* Provider: Company Two account list for the workspace returns exactly 6 active accounts, matching the 6 provisioned inboxes.
* Help center: the Billing card is a domain/inbox billing view and is explicitly not a provisioning status panel, so the count difference itself is expected; the defect is the unresolved failed domains.

## Blast radius (counted 2026-09-10)

* 7 requires_attention orders across 6 organizations hold 22 failed domains.
* 33 unconnected, never-retried inboxes on failed domains older than 7 days, across 5 organizations.

## Suggested link

Overlaps the existing DFY failed-domain master family (failed domains left claimed, un-cancellable and still billed); dedupe and parent during routing.
